My land is 8 mu. I have been doing wheat and maize on the same plots — that rotation I know well. I plant wheat in October after the maize comes off, then maize goes back in after the June harvest. I keep 5 mu for that rotation. The other 3 mu I put in cotton — it brings in more cash even though it is a lot of work in summer.

I am 58 now and my back is not what it was, but I still do what I have always done. My husband and son help during busy times.

**Wheat:** I use the improved seed the village seed shop sells, same kind I have used for years — not the expensive kind, but better than saved seed. I plough before planting because that is how I have always done autumn land. I water three times: once before the ground freezes, once when it greens up in spring, once around grain filling. I spray twice — once for weeds in winter, once for aphids in May. I put down base fertilizer when I plant and topdress urea in spring.

**Maize:** After wheat harvest I do rotary tillage and get the maize seed in fast before the rains come. Everyone here uses hybrid seed now — Zhengdan or similar, I buy whatever the shop has. Maize does not need as much water if the summer rains come, so maybe two irrigations. I spray herbicide once and watch for the worms.

**Cotton:** I plough the cotton ground in spring. I use hybrid Bt cotton — less spraying for bollworm than the old days. But I still spray four times for aphids and red spider mites. Cotton needs more water, I irrigate four times. It is heavy work picking but the price is decent.
